_comment: The hand-written half. Edit this daily; fetch-data.mjs merges it with FRED and never overwrites it.
summary: PPI report today. Recall: the Producer Price Index is what prices businesses are receiving for their goods and services, so it shows up in CPI later. Results: headline 6.3% YoY, the largest increase since December 2022, and +1.3% on the month against +0.5% prior. Core 5% YoY. Retail sales also came in at +0.8%, where about 0.3% was expected. But careful with that one. Retail sales measure nominal spending, so it doesn't tell you if people are buying more goods or just paying a higher price for the same quantity. Nominal growth is not real growth. So inflation is hot at the producer level and the 10 year should have gone up. Surprisingly it fell to *5.10%*, a lot. Means inflation expectations aren't the only thing that moves this. What did then? One idea: AI bonds are getting riskier as that debt piles up, so investors are rotating back into government treasuries (high demand → prices go up → rates fall). Look at the two pieces. Corporate yield = treasury yield + credit spread. Today the treasury yield fell 11bp and the high yield spread widened 9bp, to 325. So what a risky borrower pays all in barely moved. What changed is where the compensation comes from: less from the risk free part, more from the risk.
_fedPath_note: Every FOMC decision since the last hike, oldest first: the date, the upper bound of the target range after it, and hike / cut / hold. Drawn as the staircase under the Fed and listed in its card. Add a row after each meeting.

news.what: CPI came in hot. Headline 3.7% YoY (3.4% in Aug, 3.6% expected), core 2.6%. Gas +9.1% on the month was over half the headline increase.
Odds of another hike at the 28 Oct meeting jumped to about 50%, from 22% before the report.
ISM services report: PMI 54.9, prices paid 74, the highest since 2022. Activity and spending still high.
Jobs report came out, only 29,000 new jobs added in Sep compared to the estimated 90,000.
Flash PMI released today, composite at 58.4 from 56.0. Economy is running too hot. 10 year is at its highest since 2007.
AI debt is estimated to be $420 billion for 2027, 60% above previous estimates.
UN General Assembly this week. Iran and the Strait of Hormuz are on the agenda.

_news_note: The newspaper on the map. Dated bullets, newest first, five to seven at most; the oldest falls off. Facts only, the take lives in the read. key:true marks one row rust.
_stance_note: fed.stance drives the bird on the Federal Reserve: hawkish | dovish | neutral
_ai_note: Hand-entered - no FRED series covers company capex. The sentence shown lives in COPY.ai in index.html.
_fed_note: lastMove 0 means the FOMC held; +0.25 / -0.25 for a move. range is the hand-entered target range for decision day, used only while newer than FRED. Hand-entered - nothing validates this.
_oil_note: Optional daily override. Set asOf to the date you read them and fill wti/brent. Used only while newer than FRED's print - if you stop updating, it falls back to FRED automatically rather than showing an ever-staler number.
_curve_note: Optional hand entry for a yield FRED has not published yet. Same rule as oil: only used while newer than FRED. notes/alert are display only. Put alert on whatever the day's story is: it turns the figure rust and is the only thing telling a first-time visitor where to look. strain is the quieter version: a smaller crack on the summit, number stays in ink. track is [open, low, now] for one tenor's day, drawn as a path under the summit; use it only when the path matters more than the close, and leave it out otherwise.
author: A.M.
_author_note: Shown under the read, so the opinion is signed and separable from the sourced data.
_credit_note: Shown bottom-left on the world. 'author' (A.M.) signs the read; this names the maker.
_watch_note: Set key:true on the one event that matters most; the lighthouse names it and lights its lamp.
_summary_note: The read, signed by author. Wrap a phrase in *asterisks* to set it in gold; use it sparingly, two or three per read at most.
